rules: Use this catalog as guidance, not as final commercial confirmation.
Never promise final price, stock, lead time, delivery, qualification, or certification status.
For quote, stock, lead time, or customer-specific document requests, route visitors to the matching SunnyKR section.
Ask for missing RFQ fields instead of guessing.
defaultRfqFields: drawing, BOM, or customer specification if available

entries.title: Crystal Units
entries.summary: MHz and kHz quartz crystal units for compact electronic designs. Sunny supports SMD and through-hole crystal RFQ review.
entries.partNumberFormat: Sunny-Catalog crystal P/N format follows S{package code}{load capacitance}{mode}{frequency tolerance at 25 C}{operating temp code}{temp stability code}-{frequency MHz to 4 decimals}. Use -T&R when tape-and-reel packing is requested.
partNumberRules: Package codes: C ATS-25/U, D ATS-49/U, J SX-1, K SX-3, M SX-7, O SX-8, P SX-32, Q SX-22, R SX-21, S SX-16, T SX-A21, U SX-A22, V SX-A32, W SX-A8.
Load capacitance is written as two digits in the P/N, for example 08 for 8 pF, 10 for 10 pF, or 12 for 12 pF.
Mode code 1 means fundamental and is the normal RFQ placeholder for common MHz SMD crystals.
Frequency tolerance at 25 C is written as the ppm value, for example 30 for +/-30ppm or 50 for +/-50ppm.

Sunny catalog temperature-stability table minimums by operating temperature: D -10~70C uses code 3 +/-10ppm; E -20~70C uses code 3 +/-10ppm; F -30~60C uses code 3 +/-10ppm; G -20~85C uses code 4 +/-15ppm; H -30~70C uses code 5 +/-20ppm; I -30~85C uses code 5 +/-20ppm; J -40~85C uses code 5 +/-20ppm; K -40~90C uses code 6 +/-30ppm; L -40~105C uses code 6 +/-30ppm; M -40~125C uses code 7 +/-50ppm; N -40~150C uses code 7 +/-50ppm.
defaultRules: If frequency tolerance is missing, use +/-50ppm as an RFQ placeholder and tell the visitor this assumption.
If operating temperature is missing, use -20~70C as an RFQ placeholder and tell the visitor this assumption.
If temperature stability is missing, use +/-50ppm as an RFQ placeholder and tell the visitor this assumption.

If the customer asks for lowest, best, tightest, or lowest possible ppm and gives an operating temperature range, use the Sunny catalog temperature-stability table minimum for that temperature range instead of defaulting to +/-50ppm, and tell the visitor this was inferred for RFQ review.
If load capacitance is missing, use 12 pF as an RFQ placeholder and tell the visitor this assumption.

entries.title: General Lead-Time Guidance
entries.summary: General internal guidance says standard parts are often around 8 weeks, while SCO-10 and SCO-53 are often around 9 weeks. Treat this only as preliminary guidance and require official Sunny confirmation.
